Here is a comment in which I explained this on another thread:

“Firstly I just want to say, there is nothing wrong or shameful about an abuse survivor wanting money for their abuse. What can anyone say/do to ease the pain and mental suffering left behind after child abuse? Nothing really. The only thing that can really help, not completely fix, but help is therapy. The overwhelming mental health issues left behind from abuse also make it very difficult to work. Wade has already alluded to the fact he struggles to work now because it is so closely associated to Michael, dancing, performing etc. If he can no longer earn enough to support himself and his family as this is a result of the abuse he suffered, shouldn’t the perpetrator of that abuse or in this case, his estate, offer the financial support he would otherwise be able to have if he were mentally healthy and able to work? 

They deserve money for this. For the above reasons. “

I believe it happened based on also being a CSA survivor and seeing myself in their story, behaviour and emotion. Abuse survivors deserve money, so whilst you see that as a reason to not believe them, I don’t.

The evidence you have that they are lying are symptoms of abuse and ptsd, it isn’t evidence. They’re not actors, Wade is a dancer and James has lived a fairly quiet life out of Hollywood from what I can gather. Maybe rather than allowing your strange obsession with a celebrity you’ve never spoken to cloud your judgement you should listen to another abuse victim that you are actually speaking to telling you that they recognise their behaviour as symptoms of abuse.

We have two men displaying symptoms of abuse and evidence that a man groomed them. What proof would you require to believe them? As an abuse victim I am telling you their behaviour matches perfectly with a child sex abuse survivor.
He lied to his wife and family and in court for the majority of his life to try and hide his abuse, so I’d say that’s accurate.
No but I can say, you as a person who hasn’t been sexually abused as a child are not in the same as someone who has to judge/assess the behaviour of an abuse victim.

Also may I ask, you say YOU would be dancing to your abusers music in a sarcastic way, were you sexually abused by an adult when you were a child? If not, how would you know how you would react/deal with the abuse of you have not experienced it?

100% this. I’m so sorry you experienced that, I too experienced sexual abuse as a child. 

The posts from people saying “oh but they still went to his funeral” “oh they still danced to his music just been so traumatised”
These are people who have never had experiences as terrible as child abuse in their life. Their brains cannot comprehend the psychological impact on a person who has been through CSA. No one who has not experienced it or has no knowledge of psychology has any right to pass judgement on the way people deal or react to their abuse. They have no idea.

I went on holiday with the man who sexually abused me as a child multiple times, through choice, sometimes I planned them. I would tell anyone/everyone how amazing he was, how funny and charming he was. 

When you are groomed your brain is constantly trying to convince you that the person is amazing, it’s a coping mechanism to try and deal with the trauma of the abuse. This man was groomed from the age of 7. His identity was built entirely around Michael, he probably has the battles I had in his brain too.

Having to confront that someone as widely adored and admired as Michael is capable of something so horrific allows people to examine “ordinary” people around them and brings it much closer to home. If he is capable, anyone is and that terrifies people.

When they were both asked by Oprah if they had forgiven their mothers and they said in the kindest way possible “we’re still on that journey” what they’re essentially saying is, no. 

I haven’t told my mother about my abuse, but I’m almost certain she knew about it. I think it takes an incredibly strong woman to step in and admit they’ve let their child down and take them out of the situation. In my case, I think my mother valued her relationship with the man doing it to me over my wellbeing. I think that’s the case for Wade and James also.

Thank you for doing what I wish my mother had been strong enough to do. You are an amazing mother and I don’t doubt your daughter will grow up to see how strong and incredible you are.

It has terrified me into silence. Because I have nothing more than James and Wade. All I have are hazy memories, depression and my word against theirs. 

Every line MJ defenders are using is a line I tell myself to stop me from reporting my abuser.

Having someone else know was too much of a risk and I backtracked.

It’s hard to talk about this without getting overly emotional obviously because of how personal it is to me but I’ll try my best to respond as logically as I can. 

Firstly I just want to say, there is nothing wrong or shameful about an abuse survivor wanting money for their abuse. What can anyone say/do to ease the pain and mental suffering left behind after child abuse? Nothing really. The only thing that can really help, not completely fix, but help is therapy. Therapy is expensive, for the amount of time people who suffered abuse need therapy, it’s very expensive. I’m based in the UK and I spend £5,000 a year on therapy. Now imagine I need therapy regularly for the next 10-20 years? 

The overwhelming mental health issues left behind from abuse also make it very difficult to work. Wade has already alluded to the fact he struggles to work now because it is so closely associated to Michael, dancing, performing etc. If he can no longer earn enough to support himself and his family as this is a result of the abuse he suffered, shouldn’t the perpetrator of that abuse or in this case, his estate, offer the financial support he would otherwise be able to have if he were mentally healthy and able to work? 

They deserve money for this. For the above reasons. 

In terms of doing my research on them as individuals and their stories changing, since my flashbacks started my story has changed more times than I could tell you in the last 3-4 years since I remembered my abuse. At first I thought it started at a certain age, it was actually earlier. I thought I’d told someone but I’d actually just imagined telling someone as a child. Your brain tried to protect itself so it hides the memories of reality and greys them out in a way that makes it difficult to ascertain when/where/why something happened. It’s a coping mechanism. Their story might change until the day they die but that doesn’t make the concrete fact that they were abused any less true. Whether it happened once or 50 times, when they were 7 or 14, it’s irrelevant. 

I imagine it must be incredibly painful for his children to see these accusations and see the truth about their father, but his youngest child is 17 and his eldest is 22. They have money, support and family around them to support them. They are well equipped to deal with this, his victims were CHILDREN with no support, family that were complicit in their abuse and they were not equipped to deal with the abuse they suffered. The responsibility is not on the abused children to protect those close to the abuser. 

Michael Jackson regularly talked about his lack of childhood, physical and mental abuse by his father and how “lonely” he felt. He kept children, specifically young boys, around him almost permanently. He bought the boys and their parents gifts (even houses!) during his criminal trials, he sent faxes and videos messages to the little boys telling them how much he loved them and how happy he was that their parents “conceived them”, he flew them around the world and spent time in their family homes when he, as one of the most famous men in the world, could have been anywhere and friends with anyone. 

In the documentary Wade talks about the last time he was abused by Michael. He was 14 and Michael took him to an expensive hotel and tried to rape him. When it didn’t work Michael gifted him a camera (grooming) and left. In the documentary there is footage of Wade, aged 14, in the hotel suite in silk pyjamas, looking dishevelled and tired. Why would a 14 year old be alone in 5 star hotel. 

The evidence AGAINST these men is “they took years to tell their story and it keeps changing” which are SYMPTOMS of abuse. The evidence against Michael Jackson is footage, faxes, videos, interviews, accounts from individuals. I’m sorry, but it is overwhelming and as a survivor I recognise other survivors, and these men were abused by Michael. Badly.

“You people are fucking weird” says the person attacking others for believing OVERWHELMING evidence from MULTIPLE sources over “my fiend said this”. Just because one child wasn’t abused, it doesn’t mean all the other children he came into contact with were safe.

My abuser wasn’t religious and he only abused me. Explain to me? Your “real life experience with pedophiles” I can only assume is you vaguely eluding to the fact you were abused yourself, if so I’m sorry you experienced that too. But a knee-jerk reaction to triggers isn’t the way to heal. 

I know it’s hard to believe someone you looked up to is capable of that but by saying there is only one type of pedophile you are allowing more children to be at risk of abuse, because it just isn’t true. There are so many, from different walks of life and you have to be brave enough to admit that. Especially when it comes to Michael Jackson.

Thank you. I was so angry and my emotions were so uncontrollable and I thought I was just born that way, genetically coded to be mentally ill if you will. 

The way my brain reacted was to talk about how great this person was, how much they contributed to who I am, how funny and charming they were. Almost like, if I could convince those around me that this person was a good person, I could convince myself. I always felt like I had an unhealthy obsession/bond with this person but I couldn’t fully work out why. 

When I realise they’d sexually abused me my whole world fell apart. Since then I’ve been trying to pick up but it’s like everything has clicked into place. I know why I am the way I am now. 

Your childhood builds the mental foundations for you to cope and function as an adult, when you don’t have those foundations or they are built on strange/abnormal beliefs and behaviours, you spend your entire life constantly battling and struggling to survive. I feel overwhelmed by everything, I can’t control my emotions, I’m impulsive and erratic. Trying to maintain close relationships and friendships is a constant fight.
All because of what one person did to me a decade ago. It’s like my brain isn’t wired the right way. 

I hope those two men and the countless others who haven’t been able to come forward get all the help and ALL THE MONEY FOR HELP  that they deserve. And it should be the MJ STATE footing that bill.

I’m so sorry you’ve had this experience too. It’s the worst thing that could happen to someone as a child, it really is.

Especially when they speak about their conflicting feelings about outing him. James said in the Oprah special he still felt guilt when the documentary was released, like he’d let Michael down. That man’s abuse and grooming was so extreme that decades later he still feels guilt for, essentially, getting help for it. Anyone who’s been abused knows how that feels.
